samples.summary: `schema` calls `output()` with an unvalidated `--format` and has no try/catch, so the new throwing `default:` branch in `format()` crashes with an unhandled exception
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:26 and :33 call `output(schema, opts.format, opts.quiet)` / `output({ commands }, opts.format, opts.quiet)` inside an action with **no** `try { … } catch (e) { outputError(e, opts.quiet) }` wrapper (see the whole action, lines 10–35 — the only error path is the hand-rolled NOT_FOUND branch). Every other output()-rendering command (docs.ts:83/104/118/136/154, cells.ts:26/66/92/139, tabs.ts:16, notes.ts:43…, slides.ts:48…, api-keys.ts:20/34/48, sheets-import.ts:91) is wrapped and therefore degrades gracefully to a JSON `INVALID_FORMAT` body. `schema` instead propagates `InvalidFormatError` out of the commander action and out of `program.parse()` in packages/cli/src/bin.ts:27, where nothing catches it — `wafflebase schema --format bogus` (and `wafflebase schema docs.list --format md`) goes from printing a harmless `undefined` before this change to a Node stack trace, violating the §8.1 promise (docs/design/cli.md:723) that a bad format is reported as a structured `INVALID_FORMAT` error. Fix belongs in schema.ts: wrap the action in try/catch + `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)`.

samples.summary: `formatTable`'s new single-object branch changes `--format table` output for every existing single-record command, rendering nested fields as `[object Object]`
samples.evidence: formatTable previously returned '(no results)' for any non-array; it is a shared exported helper reached via `format()` from every command. Out-of-diff consumers whose payload is a single object now take the new `formatRecord` path: packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:26 (`schema docs.list --format table` → `parameters`/`response` are nested objects, so `String(record[k])` prints `[object Object]`; :33 prints `commands  [object Object],[object Object],…`), packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:118/104/136/154, cells.ts:26, api-keys.ts:34, sheets-import.ts:91 — all pass a server object whose nested members will stringify the same way. The change's own lessons note (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-lessons.md:27) acknowledges the `[object Object]` hazard but only `status` was flattened to scalars; the other now-affected commands were not reviewed for it.

samples.summary: User-facing docs still document the removed `*` active-workspace marker for `ctx list`
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:50 reads `# List workspaces (* = active)` immediately above `wafflebase ctx list`. `buildWorkspaceList` replaced the `*` prefix with an `active` boolean field and the default output is now JSON, so this instruction describes output the CLI no longer produces. (docs/design/cli.md:455 was updated; this published doc was not.)

samples.summary: Agent-harness comment (and its mirrored design doc) still assert that `status` ignores `--format json` and prints prose — the defect this change fixes
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:15-20 documents its whole design rationale as "`status` ignores `--format json` and prints prose (\"Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.\")… Verified empirically". The same text is duplicated at .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:18 and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1483. After this change `status --format json` emits `{ "loggedIn": false, … }`, so the stated justification for hand-parsing the session/config files is stale and will mislead the next maintainer (the workspace-resolution code itself still works, since it never actually shells out to the CLI).

samples.summary: `ctx switch` was left on the prose/`process.exit` path the new `ctx list` comment claims to match, so the two siblings now disagree
samples.evidence: ctx.ts:75-78 justifies the new structured `NOT_LOGGED_IN` error as "matching `ctx switch`", but ctx.ts:92-103 (`ctx switch`) still does `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` followed by `process.exit(1)` — plain prose, no `error.code`, no `--format` handling, and a hard `process.exit` rather than `process.exitCode`. An agent that learns to branch on `error.code === 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'` from `ctx list` gets an unparseable line from `ctx switch`; the comment in the new code also describes behaviour that does not exist.

finding.summary: `schema` calls `output()` with an unvalidated `--format` and has no try/catch, so the new throwing `default:` branch in `format()` crashes with an unhandled exception

verdict.reason: Confirmed exactly as described. formatter.ts:51-56 makes format() throw InvalidFormatError for unsupported --format values, and output() (formatter.ts:59-62) calls it unguarded. schema.ts:10-35 passes the raw opts.format straight to output() at lines 26 and 33 with no parseOutputFormat() narrowing and no try/catch — outputError is not even imported (schema.ts:3), and the only error handling is the hand-rolled NOT_FOUND branch. The global --format option in root.ts:53 has no .choices() and getGlobalOpts (root.ts:24-27) does not validate, so an arbitrary string reaches the action; bin.ts:14-27 calls program.parse() with no surrounding try/catch, so the synchronous throw escapes as an unhandled exception. The intended contract is proven by status.ts:63-70 (parseOutputFormat + try/catch + outputError), tabs.ts:18, and docs/design/cli.md:723-727 which promises a structured INVALID_FORMAT error. In-lane: changed contract of an exported symbol with an unupdated consumer; major impact (documented structured error becomes a Node stack trace on a trivially reachable path).
